title: HDMI Cables - Different Cable Types
supports: Standard cable tested for 720p/1080i; High Speed up to 10.2 Gbps (1080p, 4K30); Premium High Speed certified 18 Gbps (4K60); Ultra High Speed 48 Gbps (4K120/8K60).

title: Premium High Speed HDMI Cable certification
supports: Premium High Speed cables are tested to the full 18 Gbps for 4K@60.

title: Ultra High Speed HDMI Cable
supports: Ultra High Speed cables support up to 48 Gbps.

title: HDMI Specification 1.4b
supports: HDMI 1.4b adds 4K support (4K at up to 30 Hz).

title: HDMI Specification 2.1
supports: HDMI 2.1 up to 48 Gbps (FRL).

title: HDMI - main specifications and refresh-frequency limits tables
supports: TMDS 8b/10b coding: HDMI 1.4 max 10.2 Gbps raw = 8.16 Gbps data; HDMI 2.0 18 Gbps raw = 14.4 Gbps data; HDMI 2.1 FRL 48 Gbps raw with 16b/18b = 42.67 Gbps data; CTA-861 timings (1080p60 148.5 MHz, 4K30 297 MHz, 4K60 594 MHz).

title: DisplayPort - link rates, DP++ dual-mode, cables
supports: HBR2 4 lanes 21.6 Gbps raw = 17.28 Gbps data; HBR3 32.4 Gbps raw = 25.92 Gbps data; UHBR10 40 Gbps raw (128b/132b) = 38.69 Gbps data; DP++ passive adapters need a dual-mode source; DP8K cables certified for UHBR10.

title: DisplayPort Alt Mode over USB Type-C (USB DevDays 2019)
supports: DP Alt Mode uses up to 4 high-speed lanes of a full-featured USB Type-C cable at DP 1.4 HBR3 (8.1 Gbps/lane); 2-lane mode leaves the other pairs for USB 3.

title: Coordinated Video Timings (CVT reduced blanking)
supports: CVT-RB pixel clocks, e.g. 2560x1440@60 = 241.5 MHz; 1920x1200@60 = 154 MHz.

title: USB-C - cable types, alternate modes, power
supports: USB 2.0-only Type-C cables have no SuperSpeed pairs, so cannot carry DisplayPort Alt Mode; full-featured cables can; 3 A cables = 60 W, 5 A e-marked = 100 W (SPR), EPR cables = 240 W.

title: Thunderbolt (interface)
supports: Thunderbolt 3/4 over USB-C carries DisplayPort and USB PD up to 100 W on copper cables.

title: USB-IF Cables and Connectors
supports: Certified USB Type-C cable power ratings (60 W / 240 W logos) and data ratings.

title: USB Charger (USB Power Delivery)
supports: USB PD up to 100 W (SPR, 20 V 5 A) and up to 240 W with PD 3.1 EPR (48 V 5 A).

title: VGA connector
supports: Analog VGA commonly carries up to 1920x1200@60; quality depends on cable and converter.

title: MacBook Air (M2, 2022) - Tech Specs
supports: Two Thunderbolt/USB 4 ports with charging and DisplayPort; one external display up to 6K60; MagSafe 3; ships with 30 W or 35 W adapter; fast-charge with 70 W adapter.

title: MacBook Pro (14-inch, M3, Nov 2023) - Tech Specs
supports: Two Thunderbolt/USB 4 ports (charging, DisplayPort); HDMI output up to 4K at 120 Hz (M3); one external display up to 6K60; 70 W adapter in box; fast-charge with 96 W.

title: About the Apple USB-C Digital AV Multiport Adapter
supports: Model A2119: 3840x2160@60 with MacBook Air 2020+ and 14-inch MacBook Pro 2021+; model A1621: 3840x2160@30 and up to 1080p60.

title: Use a power adapter with your Mac
supports: Recommended adapters: MacBook Air 2022+ 30/35/67/70 W; 14-inch MacBook Pro 2021+ 67/70/96 W; any USB PD adapter can charge a USB-C Mac.

title: Fast charge your MacBook Air or MacBook Pro
supports: MacBook Air 2022+ fast charges with 67/70/96/140 W adapters + MagSafe 3 or USB-C charge cable; 14-inch MacBook Pro fast charges with 96/140 W adapters (or a display delivering 94 W).

title: USB-C to MagSafe 3 Cable (2 m)
supports: Apple USB-C to MagSafe 3 cable, used with the 140 W adapter for 16-inch MacBook Pro fast charging (see apple-fastcharge).

title: ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 11 - PSREF specifications
supports: 2x Thunderbolt 4 / USB4 (PD 3.0, DisplayPort 1.4a); 1x HDMI 2.1 up to 4K/60Hz; 45 W or 65 W USB-C adapters; Rapid Charge with 65 W.

title: Generic product class (see docs/DATA.md)
supports: A generic class whose limit is set by the standard it claims (e.g. an 'HDMI 2.0 4K60 adapter'); individual products can be worse.
